Finding submitted.

**Status: deviation** (Section 6.2(a), ¶p0283; cross-read against Section 5.2(a) ¶p0243 and the Section 6.3 indemnities ¶p0291)

**What I found**
- No aggregate monetary cap exists anywhere in the agreement (no "aggregate liability", no consequential-damages exclusion except the arbitral-panel limit in the dispute-resolution schedule). That absence benefits us as claimant, so I did not import a fees-based cap — a cap measured on the Servicing Fee would be illusory recourse for the Issuer.
- The operative limitation is a standard-of-care exculpation, and it is asymmetric: Cellco (Servicer/Marketing Agent) is liable **"only"** for willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, whereas the mirror provision for our Depositor omits "only". Combined with "All other liability is expressly waived and released", the counterparty's exculpation can be read to excuse ordinary breach of its core performance obligations (Servicer Deposit Obligation, Servicer Acquisition Obligation, remittance of Collections) — our principal recourse — which is a one-sided, effectively zero-value limitation in the counterparty's favour.

**Redline (validated, ok:true)** — smallest edit to ¶p0283: delete "only" to restore mutuality with Section 5.2(a), and add one sentence confirming that the Servicer's/Marketing Agent's specific obligations, including the Deposit and Acquisition Obligations and the Section 6.3 indemnities, sit outside any limitation or cap on liability.
